key_insight: A decoupled reinforcement-learning pipeline with a random-forest congestion detector and actor-critic controller can robustly reduce low-voltage grid violations under sparse observability.
engineering_relevance: This approach is relevant for managing PV-rich distribution grids with EV and heat-pump loads, where curative curtailment must work despite noisy measurements and imperfect grid models.
method: Random-forest pre-classifier flags likely voltage/current violations.
Actor-critic controller decides curtailment actions only when congestion is predicted.
Robustness is tested against measurement noise and grid-parameter mismatch on a real low-voltage grid.
evidence_signal: On a real low-voltage grid with synthetic future operating scenarios, the controller reduced total violation magnitude by 98.9% with accurate parameters and remained nearly unchanged under the tested noise levels.
watch_item: Performance is more sensitive to grid-model mismatch than to measurement noise, so deployment still requires careful parameter validation and model updating.
paper_title: Robustness of Reinforcement Learning-Based Congestion Management in Low-Voltage Grids
